{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZg3C_w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDH6sg", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 53, "title": "Correct Bandai 2003 RTC command completion and READY handling", "body": "## Problem

The RTC transport in `crates/ws-core/src/bus.rs` rejects control write `0x93`, although the independent mapper experiment starts command `0x13` with READY set and expects that read-only bit to be ignored.

Read completion also appears to expose an extra byte to ordinary polling software. Static inspection, unexecuted here: command `0x13` becomes READY while ACTIVE remains set; consuming its one byte starts another wait, which later exposes READY with ACTIVE clear. The inspected library reads that terminal byte too, counting two bytes instead of one. Existing tests prescribe read counts themselves and miss this failure.

These defects can stop software or misreport RTC transfers. Correct transport is a bounded prerequisite for equipped-cartridge support; commercial-game impact remains unmeasured.

## Expected outcome

The existing Bandai 2003 CA/CB interface completes commands `0x10–0x1B` with the independently specified host byte counts, supports the terminal read byte correctly, and ignores the read-only READY bit when starting a supported command.

Preserve absent-chip `0xFF` data and existing mapper availability. This task corrects transport; equipped-cartridge detection, calendar progression, persistence and cartridge IRQ integration remain material gaps.

## Context

Baseline: `75f0ebedc424a614660320d9f5a7696f1af1e0b6`. Relevant paths include `bus.rs` command/read/tick handling, its absent-RTC test, `fixtures/compat.asm`, `crates/ws-core/tests/compat.rs`, and production browser compatibility scripts.

The pinned [mapper experiment](https://github.com/asiekierka/ws-test-suite/blob/5d8950d6b271a585c252af3ced93fbd2045f4752/src/mono/rtc/mapper/main.c) specifies host counts for commands `10–1B`: `1,1,1,1,7,7,3,3,2,2,2,2`, and checks READY clearing on `0x93`. Its configuration requests mapper 2003 and an RTC; inspected source is experimental evidence, without an inspected console pass log. Applying mapper-controlled transfer counts to the absent-chip path is an explicit architectural inference.

The pinned [library routines](https://github.com/WonderfulToolchain/target-wswan-syslibs/blob/b3f2366c458421775cc4a18b4925d12a8d9c058b/libws/src/cart/cart_rtc.c) establish preloaded first writes and polling that consumes READY data before checking ACTIVE. [Register definitions](https://github.com/WonderfulToolchain/hardware-definitions/blob/46783132a59e576c11456f5997620594eca1c390/target/wswan/cart/rtc.xml) identify CA/CB and control bits.

Correction record: replace the earlier assumptions that reset implies zero host bytes, terminal READY represents an additional byte, and setting READY makes an otherwise supported command invalid. Use the experiment's host counts and library completion protocol. The [S-3511A manufacturer manual, §2](https://www.rockby.com.au/DSheets/10110.pdf) makes reset's R/W bit irrelevant; chip reset semantics must remain distinct from mapper host-transfer counting. A reset host byte does not imply a writable chip payload.

Exact silicon latency remains unestablished. Retain the existing 64-clock scheduled-stage approximation and label it honestly. Preserve explicit handling of unsupported commands; do not expand uncertain commands or copy another emulator.

Saved [Issue #51 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/75f0ebedc424a614660320d9f5a7696f1af1e0b6/docs/issue-51-validation.md) reports native and complete production Chromium suites passing. Those results were not rerun during planning and do not establish RTC protocol correctness or commercial compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Correct supported CA/CB transactions so independent polling routines observe the literal counts above. A read's terminal READY exposes its final byte; consuming it clears READY without scheduling a phantom byte. Preserve preloaded first writes, command readback and absent-chip `0xFF` data. `0x93` starts the same supported command as `0x13`, with READY initially cleared.
- [ ] Add independent register-level tests covering every supported command, read/write completion, terminal consumption, consecutive commands, READY masking, and reset host counting. Expected counts/status vectors must not come from production command tables. Record focused baseline failures for read overcounting and `0x93` rejection, then corrected passes.
- [ ] Cover emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations and supported mono/Color modes. Test delayed readiness around the retained clock boundary, equivalent partitioned clock advances, and restart/model-change cancellation of pending transport without damaging cartridge saves or console EEPROM. Preserve ordinary CPU I/O accounting and shared audio, timer, video and DMA progression.
- [ ] Add an original source-included cartridge through the existing fixture generator. Execute bounded polling loops through normal CPU IN/OUT instructions and assert CPU-written counts, completion status and absent data against independent literals natively and through the production Chromium/Wasm player on all three models, supported runtime mode transitions, and fresh restart. Poison stale completion records so retained saves cannot satisfy success.
- [ ] Before merge, pass `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `git diff --check`. In `web`, pass `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, then complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` sequentially against the production preview.
- [ ] Preserve existing CPU, three-model, firmware-free startup, graphics/input/frame, audio/PCM, GDMA/SDMA/Hyper Voice, SRAM/cartridge EEPROM/internal EEPROM, Wasm/browser lifecycle and save-integrity acceptance. Keep ROM identity, ownership/provenance and browser-local persistence behavior intact; require no proprietary ROM or firmware.
- [ ] Update hardware support, source reconciliation, fixture provenance and validation documentation. Record old assumptions, corrected requirements, rationale, actual failures/passes and unperformed checks. The Coordinator reviews the final change against every criterion before merge; document remaining RTC attachment/calendar/IRQ gaps without claiming broad commercial readiness.

## Optional validation

Run baseline production-browser discrimination or additional browser engines. Compare separately available original-console observations if useful; no such measurements or human gameplay were performed during planning, and neither is a prerequisite.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.

This autonomous campaign has no human-approval gate. Mandatory acceptance uses
automated native and production-browser tests on the emulator's supported model
and mode configurations. Physical-console measurements and human gameplay are
optional evidence and must remain explicitly unperformed unless actually available.
Do not invent device identities, real-device results or a requirement for human
confirmation. Resolve technical errors with recorded evidence and automated checks
through the existing Coordinator workflow.
